chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sulaym, the mawla of Tarbal, from Hisham al-Jawaleeqi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Glorified be Allah' — what does He mean by it? He said: Extolment (Tanzih).
ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of 'Subhan Allah' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'Subhan Allah' as 'Tanzih', emphasizing the absolute transcendence of Allah by absolving Him of any defects or imperfections. This concise definition anchors the Shia theological understanding of divine purity, distinguishing it from mere praise by focusing on the negation of limitations. It serves as a foundational concept for understanding how believers articulate God's unique nature in worship and creed.
